theme.title: Mixed / Stock-Picker's Market
theme.summary: Health Care (+2.37%) and Real Estate (+1.88%) led the market today, while Technology (-0.40%) and Industrials (+0.07%) brought up the rear. That split lines up with a rotation out of growth: growth-oriented sectors averaged +0.20% versus +1.32% for defensives and +0.78% for value and cyclicals, suggesting money moved from high-multiple names into steadier, cash-generative businesses. That shows up at the index level too: the blue-chip Dow gained +1.02% while the tech-heavy Nasdaq fell -0.02%, a wide enough gap to matter. Small caps bucked the broader trend, with the Russell 2000 up +1.65%, outperforming large caps. The VIX fell 6.08% to 17.31, which reads as an orderly rotation rather than panic-driven selling. Gold slipped 0.74% to $4,134.60, crude oil was little changed at $98.32, and bitcoin gained 1.23% — cross-asset moves weren't all pointing the same direction as equities.
